neuroplasticity.title: Neuroplasticity
neuroplasticity.subtitle: Track infant brain plasticity peaks with myelination waves
neuroplasticity.myelinationDesc: Myelin sheath formation around nerve fibers. More myelin = faster signal transmission. Track the progress of neural insulation development.
neuroplasticity.pruningDesc: Weak neural connections are eliminated to make room for stronger ones. This process optimizes brain efficiency after critical periods close.
neuroplasticity.languageDesc: The language window (0-12 months) is the most intensive period for speech and language development. Babies are attuned to the sounds and rhythms of their native language from birth.
neuroplasticity.languageWhy: Brain circuits for language are being hardwired during this period. By 12 months, the brain has already begun to prune connections not used for the native language, making early exposure crucial.
neuroplasticity.languageMyelination: Language pathways (Wernicke's and Broca's areas) are rapidly myelinating from 0-12 months. Myelination enables the rapid sequential processing needed for speech comprehension and production.
neuroplasticity.languagePruning: By 12 months, pruning of non-native sound discrimination begins. By 18 months, the ability to distinguish foreign language sounds is significantly reduced without exposure.
neuroplasticity.visualDesc: The vision window (0-4 months) is critical for developing eye coordination, depth perception, and visual acuity. The visual cortex develops rapidly during this period.
neuroplasticity.visualWhy: Binocular vision (using both eyes together) must be established during this window. After 4 months, visual cortex plasticity decreases significantly, making late intervention less effective.
neuroplasticity.visualMyelination: The visual cortex and optic radiations are rapidly myelinating from birth. By 4 months, basic visual processing pathways are largely insulated and functional.
neuroplasticity.visualPruning: After 4 months, visual cortex pruning accelerates. Redundant visual connections are eliminated, optimizing for the specific visual environment the baby experiences.
neuroplasticity.motorDesc: The motor window (2-9 months) covers the development of both gross and fine motor skills. From head control to reaching, grasping, and eventually crawling.
neuroplasticity.motorWhy: Motor cortex development requires intense practice during this window. Neural pathways for movement are being established and refined through repeated use.
neuroplasticity.motorMyelination: Motor cortex and corticospinal tracts are myelinating from 2-9 months. Myelination enables the precise, coordinated movements needed for voluntary motor control.
neuroplasticity.motorPruning: After 9 months, motor pruning focuses on eliminating unused motor pathways. Intensive practice during the window strengthens the connections that survive pruning.
neuroplasticity.sensoryIntegrationDesc: The sensory integration window (0-36 months) encompasses all five senses integrating with motor, language, and cognitive development. This is the broadest developmental window.
neuroplasticity.sensoryIntegrationWhy: Multisensory integration is foundational for all higher brain functions. The brain learns to combine input from different senses to create a coherent picture of the world.
neuroplasticity.sensoryMyelination: Sensory integration pathways across all cortex regions are myelinating throughout this window. Association areas connecting different sensory modalities develop last.
neuroplasticity.sensoryPruning: Pruning of sensory connections continues through age 3. The brain eliminates sensory connections not regularly activated, optimizing for the baby's specific sensory environment.
neuroplasticity.gutBrainAxisDesc: The gut-brain axis window (0-12 months) tracks the bidirectional communication between gut health and brain development. The vagus nerve provides a direct gut-brain connection.
neuroplasticity.gutBrainAxisWhy: Gut health directly influences brain development through the microbiome-gut-brain axis. Inflammation in the gut can affect behavior, sleep, and neurological development.
neuroplasticity.gutMyelination: The vagus nerve and enteric nervous system pathways are myelinating from birth. Gut-brain communication requires this myelin for rapid signal transmission.
neuroplasticity.gutPruning: Gut-brain axis pruning correlates with gut microbiome establishment. By 12 months, the gut-brain connection patterns are largely stabilized.

teething.title: Teething
teething.subtitle: Track teeth & comfort symptomsy
teething.symptomDroolingDesc: Excessive saliva production — very common during teething.
teething.symptomGumSwollenDesc: Red, inflamed gums at the eruption site.
teething.symptomIrritableDesc: Fussy, crying more than usual due to gum discomfort.
teething.symptomBitingDesc: Chewing on toys, fingers, or anything within reach.
teething.symptomSleepDisruptedDesc: Frequent night wakings due to pain.
teething.symptomRashDesc: Red rash on chin/neck from excess drool.
teething.symptomAppetiteDesc: Reluctance to eat due to sore gums.
teething.teethingRingNote: Silicone or rubber ring — chill in fridge (not freezer). The counter-pressure and cold soothe gums.
teething.coldWashclothNote: Wet a clean washcloth, twist and freeze 30 mins. The texture and cold provide relief.
teething.gumMassageNote: Use a clean finger to gently rub the gum for 1-2 minutes. Works quickly for immediate relief.
teething.chilledFeederNote: Fill a mesh feeder with frozen fruit or breast milk. Baby chews safely while getting cold relief.
teething.painReliefOTCNote: Acetaminophen (Tylenol) or ibuprofen (Motrin) for babies 6+ months. Always consult your doctor first.
teething.amberBeadNote: Baltic amber contains succinic acid said to reduce inflammation. Use with supervision and never on a string around neck.
teething.otcDosageNote: Consult your pediatrician before giving any medication to babies under 6 months.
teething.tipFrozenRingBody: Freeze a silicone teething ring for 30 mins. The cold numbs gums safely. Never freeze gel-filled rings.
teething.tipBitingBody: Baby's gums are inflamed — biting applies counter-pressure. Offer cold washcloths, silicone toys, or wooden teethers.
teething.tipDroolRashBody: Excess drool causes chin/neck rash. Pat dry frequently, apply petroleum jelly as barrier, keep a soft bib on.
teething.tipFeverBody: Teething may cause slight fever (<38°C / 100.4°F). Higher fevers are NOT normal — consult your doctor.
teething.tipNightWakingBody: Teething pain peaks at night. Try cold gum massage before bed, and keep the room cool (68-72°F / 20-22°C).
teething.tipFirstToothBody: Start brushing when first tooth erupts. Use a tiny smear of fluoride toothpaste on a soft infant toothbrush.

criticalPeriods.title: Critical Periods
criticalPeriods.subtitle: Sensitive windows in your baby's first year
criticalPeriods.signs: Signs Baby Is In This Period
criticalPeriods.attachmentDesc: The attachment window (0-6 months) is when your baby forms their primary bond with caregivers. Consistent responsive care builds secure attachment which supports emotional regulation throughout life.
criticalPeriods.attachmentWhy: Secure attachment formed in this window predicts better relationships, emotional resilience, and reduced anxiety later in childhood. This is the foundation for all future social-emotional development.
criticalPeriods.languageDesc: The language critical period (0-12 months) spans the entire first year. Your baby is absorbing all sounds, rhythms, and word patterns from their native language environment.
criticalPeriods.languageWhy: Babies can distinguish all human sounds in the first 6 months. By 12 months, the brain begins pruning language sounds it hasn't heard. Early rich language input shapes neural pathways for all future communication.
criticalPeriods.motorDesc: The motor window (2-9 months) covers the emergence of head control through crawling. Gross motor milestones build sequentially — each skill provides the foundation for the next.
criticalPeriods.motorWhy: Motor development and brain development are tightly coupled. Movement allows babies to explore, which drives cognitive development. Tummy time strengthens neck muscles needed for sitting, reaching, and eventually walking.
criticalPeriods.visualDesc: The visual critical period (0-4 months) is when visual neural pathways develop most rapidly. High-contrast patterns and face-to-face interaction are essential visual stimulation during this window.
criticalPeriods.visualWhy: Babies are born with immature visual systems. During this window, the brain is rapidly building pathways for depth perception, focus, and color vision. Visual stimulation directly shapes the developing visual cortex.
criticalPeriods.gutMicrobiomeDesc: The gut microbiome window (0-6 months) is when the bacterial ecosystem in your baby's gut is established. This ecosystem influences digestion, immunity, and increasingly, brain development.
criticalPeriods.gutMicrobiomeWhy: 80% of the immune system resides in the gut. The first 6 months of bacterial colonization sets the trajectory for immune health, allergy risk, and even mood regulation through the gut-brain axis.
criticalPeriods.gutBrainAxisDesc: The gut-brain axis window (0-12 months) tracks the bidirectional communication between gut health and brain development. Feeding patterns, gut flora, and digestion all influence neurological development.
criticalPeriods.gutBrainAxisWhy: The vagus nerve connects gut and brain directly. Gut inflammation can affect behavior and sleep. Conversely, brain development affects digestion. Optimizing gut health supports both physical and neurological development.

sensoryIntegration.correlationVestibularProprioceptiveDesc: Balance and body awareness work together for coordination and movement planning.
sensoryIntegration.correlationTactileOralDesc: Touch exploration through hands and mouth are deeply connected in early sensory development.
sensoryIntegration.correlationVisualAuditoryDesc: Seeing and hearing together enable language development and social referencing.
sensoryIntegration.correlationProprioceptiveTactileDesc: Body-in-space awareness combined with touch enables precise object manipulation.
sensoryIntegration.correlationVestibularVisualDesc: Balance system supports visual tracking and eye-hand coordination.
sensoryIntegration.tactileDesc: Touch processing — how baby responds to physical contact, textures, and temperature.
sensoryIntegration.tactile02mDesc: Baby responds to gentle touch, warmth, and cradling. Rooting and grasp reflexes are active.
sensoryIntegration.tactile24mDesc: Baby reaches for objects, explores textures with hands, and shows interest in different surfaces.
sensoryIntegration.tactile46mDesc: Baby brings objects to mouth, explores food textures, and differentiates between smooth and rough.
sensoryIntegration.tactile612mDesc: Baby seeks different textures actively, uses pincer grasp, and tolerates messy play.
sensoryIntegration.vestibularDesc: Balance and movement processing — how baby responds to changes in position and motion.
sensoryIntegration.vestibular03mDesc: Baby calms to gentle rocking, responds to tilting, and head lag decreases.
sensoryIntegration.vestibular36mDesc: Baby initiates rolling, enjoys being tilted, and develops head control when upright.
sensoryIntegration.vestibular612mDesc: Baby pulls to stand, cruises furniture, and adapts posture to uneven surfaces.
sensoryIntegration.proprioceptiveDesc: Body awareness — sensing where body parts are in space without looking.
sensoryIntegration.proprioceptive03mDesc: Baby moves arms and legs symmetrically, responds to positioning, and startles to own movements.
sensoryIntegration.proprioceptive36mDesc: Baby reaches intentionally, kicks both legs equally, and brings hands to midline.
sensoryIntegration.proprioceptive612mDesc: Baby crawls with reciprocal leg movement, pulls to stand, and throws objects intentionally.
sensoryIntegration.visualDesc: Sight processing — how baby focuses, tracks, and interprets visual information.
sensoryIntegration.visual02mDesc: Baby focuses on faces at 20cm, follows objects past midline, and recognizes caregiver faces.
sensoryIntegration.visual24mDesc: Baby follows moving objects 180 degrees, reaches for bright toys, and shows interest in mirrors.
sensoryIntegration.visual48mDesc: Baby develops depth perception, looks for dropped objects, and actively studies pictures.
sensoryIntegration.visual812mDesc: Baby points to objects of interest, identifies familiar pictures, and watches how things work.
sensoryIntegration.auditoryDesc: Sound processing — how baby responds to, differentiates, and interprets sounds.
sensoryIntegration.auditory03mDesc: Baby startles to loud sounds, calms to familiar voice, and turns toward sound sources.
sensoryIntegration.auditory36mDesc: Baby responds to own name, laughs at peek-a-boo, and vocalizes in response to music.
sensoryIntegration.auditory612mDesc: Baby understands 'no', turns to sounds out of sight, and babbles with intonation.
sensoryIntegration.oralMotorDesc: Mouth and face sensation — feeding, chewing, and verbal development.
sensoryIntegration.oralMotor03mDesc: Baby has strong suck reflex, roots when touched around mouth, and coordinates suck-swallow-breathe.
sensoryIntegration.oralMotor36mDesc: Baby opens mouth for spoon, chews on toys, and mouthing exploration is active.
sensoryIntegration.oralMotor612mDesc: Baby brings food to mouth, chews with up-and-down motion, and drinks from cup with help.
sensoryIntegration.interoceptiveDesc: Internal body awareness — hunger, fullness, thirst, pain, and emotion recognition.
sensoryIntegration.interoceptive06mDesc: Baby shows hunger and fullness cues, calms with consistent routines, and differentiates discomfort types.
sensoryIntegration.interoceptive612mDesc: Baby shows awareness of wet/dirty diaper, points to hurt body part, and shows clear emotions.
